events.excerpt: Whether it's nostalgia or a sense that technology has gotten a bit too pervasive, there’s no denying that Slate Auto appears to be tuned into the particular moment. The startup has a simple pitch : an affordable electric truck with just the basics , leaving owners to DIY and BYOD for everything else, all for a sub-$25,000 starting price. Among the things Slate does without is an embedded infotainment system. The small digital display on the dashboard that shows your speed and range is also where the backup camera appears if you engage reverse, and there are two USB-C ports that provide power but not connectivity, and that’s that. But there is a solution to getting lost, and it's called “Screenless GPS.” Even though we don’t have a Slate truck to test it with, the OEM sent us a unit to review. That’s right, it’s a good old spiral-bound road atlas! “We believe you should use the devices you know and love,” Slate says, and it reckons that maps worked just fine for past generations, so they should still work now. Read full article Comments
events.headline: Screenless GPS: Slate Auto says, "Remember the road atlas"

events.excerpt: It's a story as old as time. Billionaire nerd boy meets girl. Girl is later suspected of being a spy. News at 11. Oh, and it's also been reported that he was having an affair with one of his direct-report employees. When Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang makes a "romantic" blunder, he doesn't do it halfway. The boss of the world's most valuable company – well, it was until recently, anyway – publicly resigned yesterday, November 12, as CEO, president, and board member, effective immediately. We don't know if he jumped or if he was pushed. He left after admitting to having an affair. Although he never named an affair partner, one of the affairs was reported to be with Alice Huang, AKA Huang Le. She's head of the Chinese company Megaspeed, which was an Nvidia partner. Megaspeed is accused of being a front for China's government that was used to transfer Nvidia chips to China, although this hasn't been proven. Some US officials also suspect [PDF] she's working for Chinese intelligence, although the DoJ said it hasn't yet reached a conclusion about this. The final nail in Jensen's coffin came when The New York Times reported he had also allegedly had an affair with Nvidia's VP of health care, Kimberly Powell. Jeeze, guy! In the aftermath, Nvidia's CFO, Colette Kress, was appointed interim CEO.
events.headline: Most affairs don't matter except to the people involved. Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen's blunder will rock the world

events.excerpt: For people who are blind or visually impaired, navigating a busy city street can be difficult, even with the help of a white cane or guide dog. But what if you could sense nearby obstacles through vibrations on your skin? That's the idea behind a project by YouTuber DebackTech, who has developed an experimental pair of smart glasses that use LiDAR sensors and a vibration-equipped shirt to give wearers a sense of their surroundings without relying on sight. The plan is to give visually impaired individuals a sense of spatial awareness without resorting to cameras, audio cues, or any bulky equipment. DebackTech set out with two specific goals in mind: navigating a crowded city street without sight and catching a ball while blindfolded. The project started with a small 64-point LiDAR sensor, which measures distances by emitting light and detecting its reflections. DebackTech found that the resolution of this sensor was too low to be of much use, so he switched to a 512-point sensor and mounted three of them on a pair of glasses. An inertial measurement unit (IMU) was also added to track head movements and orientation. events.headline: Turning Sight Into Touch with DIY Smart Glasses

events.excerpt: ANTALYA, Turkey—Amid upbeat green-tech pep talks and notices for happy hours at the annual United Nations COP31 climate change conference on Thursday, two new reports offered a stark reminder of how far the world remains from containing global warming. Climate Action Tracker , a nonprofit group that analyzes climate policies, found that the planet is still on track to warm nearly 5° Fahrenheit by 2100, a rise that would devastate coral reefs, disrupt agriculture and forests and melt most of the world’s ice. In a separate bulletin, the European Union’s Copernicus climate change service reported that global warming has accelerated significantly since the 2015 Paris climate agreement . When the Paris agreement was adopted, the average global temperature was projected to surpass the pact’s long-term threshold of 2.7° Fahrenheit above the preindustrial average around 2045. After another decade of global climate summits, warming is now projected to cross that benchmark as soon as 2029, according to Copernicus. Read full article Comments
events.headline: Scientists warn 1.5°C climate change threshold could arrive by 2029

Its language backbone has 48 mixture-of-experts decoder layers, each routing tokens to 8 of 384 experts, for 594B total and 17B active parameters. events.excerpt: Microsoft is retiring some legacy layout settings in Word, potentially rearranging documents created or last saved in Word 2010 or earlier. "Affected documents may show layout differences, such as text reflow, changes in spacing or page count, or images and shapes moving to another page," the Windows biz said . The advice, if silly little things like page layout in a document matter, is to "consider exporting it to PDF before the change." Compatibility Mode lets a newer version of Word open a document created in an older version, such as Word 2010, without changing its layout. Newer features are switched off while the document is open this way. Users can convert the document to unlock newer features, although people using older versions of Word may then have difficulty editing parts of it. Microsoft has not identified the individual settings being retired, saying only: "We are retiring a set of compatibility options in Microsoft Word (desktop app) for documents in Compatibility Mode." The reason? "To simplify how Word handles document layout and provide a more consistent experience across platforms." events.excerpt: gm Zcash community. We’ve just submitted our latest retroactive grant application covering the work we’ve been doing on Unstoppable Wallet for iOS and Android. And there’s something pretty cool we want to show you. Zcash wallet sync went from hours to minutes. Seriously. We integrated the new Slipstream sync engine and ran a benchmark on an iPhone 17 Pro, restoring a Zcash wallet with 1.35 million blocks of history. Here’s what happened: Old sync engine: ~3 hours 28 minutes Slipstream: 9 minutes 43 seconds That’s ~21x faster. Not a typo. To be precise, Slipstream completed the full sync twice (9:43 and 9:45). events.excerpt: South Korea said on Friday that Google had met the safety rules for sending detailed maps of the country overseas. This brings Google closer to offering full navigation services after 19 years of disputes with the South Korean government. South Korea’s Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport said on Friday that a team of government officials and outside experts had confirmed Google followed the security rules, according to the Korea Herald. The team checked whether Google had met the conditions set on February 27, when South Korea allowed it to send highly detailed maps of the country overseas. These maps use a 1:5,000 scale, meaning they show much more detail than regular maps. Google submitted its final report on November 4. As part of the changes, Google removed information showing exact locations in South Korea from Google Maps and Google Earth. This applies to both the websites and the Android and iPhone apps. Google also added a system that blocks app updates if they include location details that are not allowed. This is meant to stop the removed information from appearing again.
